messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, an 85-year-old male, was admitted to the hospital with bilateral foot swelling, decreased urine output, and a poor urinary stream. He also complained of breathlessness, anorexia, weight loss, and had a past medical history significant for anemia. Physical examination revealed multiple, nontender, firm lymph nodes in the right upper jugular, middle jugular, right and left submandibular, and multiple right-sided axillary lymph nodes. His laboratory investigations revealed findings consistent with tumor lysis syndrome, including elevated uric acid, hyperphosphatemia, and hypocalcemia. Bone marrow examination showed hypercellular smears with reduced megakaryocytes and erythropoiesis. The bone marrow differential counts revealed immature cells with monocytic differentiation and large collections of mature lymphocytes.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
Despite being explained about the treatment options and prognosis, the patient refused to undergo any further investigations and therapy.

Discharge Condition:
The patient was discharged home in fair condition. A follow-up plan was initiated with further medical management as an outpatient.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was chiefly caused by an acute leukaemia with monocytic differentiation (immature monocytic cells in the marrow) presenting with spontaneous tumour lysis syndrome; the large collections of mature lymphocytes suggest coexisting CLL. Because the diagnosis section is withheld, choosing the monocytic leukaemia as principal is a judgement call, on the basis that the high-turnover acute process best explains the tumour lysis. Its neoplasm is in chapter C, category C93 (monocytic leukaemia).

CODE: C93
